title: Pulsar Dust Extraction
description: This simulation models the process of extracting and refining pulsar dust from raw stellar-ice core samples. Pulsar dust is a highly energetic material with applications in advanced power systems.
objective: To extract and refine highly energetic pulsar dust from raw stellar-ice core samples to a purity of 99.9% or higher.
principles: The extraction leverages the high magnetic susceptibility of pulsar dust to separate it from the non-magnetic stellar ice. Further purification is achieved through centrifugal separation based on density and laser ablation of remaining micro-impurities.

steps.title: Core Fragmentation
steps.action: Use a high-frequency sonic drill to fracture the raw stellar-ice core into manageable fragments.
steps.detail: This initial step exposes the embedded pulsar dust particles, maximizing the surface area for the subsequent magnetic separation.

steps.title: Magnetic Sieving
steps.action: Pass the fragmented ice through a series of increasingly powerful magnetic sieves.
steps.detail: The pulsar dust, being highly magnetic, will adhere to the sieves while the non-magnetic ice particles pass through. This is the primary separation method.

steps.title: Centrifugal Separation
steps.action: The collected dust is mixed with a dense, inert liquid and spun in a high-G centrifuge.
steps.detail: The heavier pulsar dust is forced to the bottom of the centrifuge tubes, separating it from any lighter impurities that were collected along with the dust.

steps.title: Laser Refining
steps.action: The semi-purified dust is spread into a thin layer and bombarded with a precisely tuned laser.
steps.detail: The laser is calibrated to a frequency that vaporizes any remaining non-pulsar impurities, leaving behind the pure, refined pulsar dust.

steps.title: Purity Analysis
steps.action: Use a mass spectrometer to analyze the purity of the refined dust.
steps.detail: The purity must be above 99.9% to be considered stable and safe for use in advanced power systems. If purity is insufficient, the laser refining step must be repeated.

steps.title: Energetic Containment
steps.action: The final product is stored in a magnetically shielded, vacuum-sealed container.
steps.detail: This prevents energy leakage and decay of the highly energetic material. Failure to contain it properly can result in a significant energy release.

tips: The strength of the magnetic sieves must be carefully calibrated to avoid magnetizing the ice fragments themselves.
The laser refiner's frequency is the most critical variable. An incorrect frequency can destroy the pulsar dust along with the impurities.
